scenes.tts: The lamp is outside the cells. How does each cell record where it sits?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Cells' Own Record. One progenitor on the sheet, with a nucleus. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: The lamp is outside the cells. How does each cell record where it sits?

scenes.tts: Inside the cells, position is recorded as levels of transcription factors, proteins that switch genes on or off.
scenes.visual: Inside the nucleus, proteins bind DNA.
scenes.narration: Inside the cells, position is recorded as levels of transcription factors, proteins that switch genes on or off.

scenes.tts: Two of them run in opposite directions along the front-to-back axis.
scenes.visual: Two opposing ramps across the dorsal map.
scenes.narration: Two of them run in opposite directions along the front-to-back axis.

scenes.tts: E M X two is highest at the back. Pax six is highest at the front.
scenes.caption: Emx2 is highest at the back. Pax6 is highest at the front.
scenes.visual: One ramp labelled Emx2, rising toward the back; the other labelled Pax6, rising toward the front.
scenes.narration: Emx2 is highest at the back. Pax6 is highest at the front.

scenes.tts: Each also varies from the midline outward, and two more factors join them.
scenes.visual: A four-point compass appears: Emx2 back and medial, Pax6 front and lateral, COUP-TFI back and lateral, Sp8 front and medial.
scenes.narration: Each also varies from the midline outward, and two more factors join them.

scenes.tts: The levels of these proteins are each progenitor's record of where it sits.
scenes.visual: Each cell shows a small bar chart of its four levels, different at each position.
scenes.narration: The levels of these proteins are each progenitor's record of where it sits.

scenes.tts: The record and the lamp are linked. Changing F G F eight shifts the gradients. Whether E M X two acts back on it is still argued.
scenes.caption: The record and the lamp are linked. Changing FGF8 shifts the gradients. Whether Emx2 acts back on it is still argued.
scenes.visual: A solid arrow runs from the lamp at the front to the Emx2 ramp; a dashed arrow runs back, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: The record and the lamp are linked. Changing FGF8 shifts the gradients. Whether Emx2 acts back on it is still argued.

scenes.tts: A gradient alone is only a correlation. So run both tests: remove the factor, then add more.
scenes.visual: The two test cards from the last chapter return: remove, add.
scenes.narration: A gradient alone is only a correlation. So run both tests: remove the factor, then add more.

scenes.tts: E M X two is highest at the back. Delete it. Which way should the borders move, and which areas should grow?
scenes.caption: Emx2 is highest at the back. Delete it. Which way should the borders move, and which areas should grow?
scenes.visual: The Emx2 ramp fades away. The map waits. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Emx2 is highest at the back. Delete it. Which way should the borders move, and which areas should grow?

scenes.tts: The borders move back. The front-and-middle areas grow, and the visual area shrinks.
scenes.visual: Borders slide back: motor and somatosensory spread backward, visual shrinks.
scenes.narration: The borders move back. The front-and-middle areas grow, and the visual area shrinks.

scenes.tts: In two thousand, Kathie Bishop, Guy Goudreau and Dennis O'Leary found this in mice lacking E M X two.
scenes.caption: In 2000, Kathie Bishop, Guy Goudreau and Dennis O'Leary found this in mice lacking Emx2.
scenes.visual: On screen: Bishop, Goudreau and O'Leary, 2000. Marker borders shown shifted back.
scenes.narration: In 2000, Kathie Bishop, Guy Goudreau and Dennis O'Leary found this in mice lacking Emx2.

scenes.tts: Without working Pax six, the shift went the other way. Front areas shrank, and the visual area grew forward.
scenes.caption: Without working Pax6, the shift went the other way. Front areas shrank, and the visual area grew forward.
scenes.visual: The Pax6 ramp fades; borders slide forward instead.
scenes.narration: Without working Pax6, the shift went the other way. Front areas shrank, and the visual area grew forward.

scenes.tts: Now raise E M X two everywhere, keeping its slope. What would show that it allocates territory?
scenes.caption: Now raise Emx2 everywhere, keeping its slope. What would show that it allocates territory?
scenes.visual: The Emx2 ramp lifts with the same slope. A dashed outline marks the whole cortex. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now raise Emx2 everywhere, keeping its slope. What would show that it allocates territory?

scenes.tts: The map should move the opposite way, with the whole cortex about the same size.
scenes.visual: Borders slide forward; the dashed outline keeps its size.
scenes.narration: The map should move the opposite way, with the whole cortex about the same size.

scenes.tts: In two thousand four, Tadashi Hamasaki and colleagues in O'Leary's laboratory found this.
scenes.caption: In 2004, Tadashi Hamasaki and colleagues in O'Leary's laboratory found this.
scenes.visual: On screen: Hamasaki and colleagues, 2004.
scenes.narration: In 2004, Tadashi Hamasaki and colleagues in O'Leary's laboratory found this.

scenes.tts: The visual area grew and the front areas shrank. Total cortical area did not change significantly.
scenes.visual: Visual expands, front shrinks, total outline unchanged.
scenes.narration: The visual area grew and the front areas shrank. Total cortical area did not change significantly.

scenes.tts: Loss and gain move the borders in opposite directions. That is strong evidence for allocating territory, not simply permitting cortex to exist.
scenes.visual: Two arrows, one each way. On screen: loss and gain, opposite directions.
scenes.narration: Loss and gain move the borders in opposite directions. That is strong evidence for allocating territory, not simply permitting cortex to exist.

scenes.tts: Coop T F one tells a similar story for loss.
scenes.caption: COUP-TFI tells a similar story for loss.
scenes.visual: A table begins to build, row by row. Row one: Emx2.
scenes.narration: COUP-TFI tells a similar story for loss.

scenes.tts: In two thousand seven, Michèle Studer's laboratory removed it from cortex alone.
scenes.caption: In 2007, Michèle Studer's laboratory removed it from cortex alone.
scenes.visual: Row two: COUP-TFI, cortex-only knockout, 2007.
scenes.narration: In 2007, Michèle Studer's laboratory removed it from cortex alone.

scenes.tts: Frontal motor areas spread across most of the sheet, and the sensory areas were squeezed toward the back.
scenes.visual: On the map, motor cortex spreads over most of the sheet; sensory areas crowd at the back.
scenes.narration: Frontal motor areas spread across most of the sheet, and the sensory areas were squeezed toward the back.

scenes.tts: Pax six is the cautionary case. In two thousand seven, David Price's group raised it up to three times normal.
scenes.caption: Pax6 is the cautionary case. In 2007, David Price's group raised it up to three times normal.
scenes.visual: Row three: Pax6. The Pax6 ramp lifts. On screen: up to 3× normal.
scenes.narration: Pax6 is the cautionary case. In 2007, David Price's group raised it up to three times normal.

scenes.tts: The map barely moved.
scenes.visual: Borders hold still. The raise-it cell for Pax6 stays flat.
scenes.narration: The map barely moved.

scenes.tts: A knockout limited to cortex shifted the markers. Yet the area-specific connections with the thalamus stayed normal.
scenes.visual: Marker borders slide, while thalamic axons still land in their usual places. On screen: 2008.
scenes.narration: A knockout limited to cortex shifted the markers. Yet the area-specific connections with the thalamus stayed normal.

scenes.tts: So Pax six may bias how markers are expressed more than it decides where an area sits. But in twenty thirteen, a cortex-only knockout shrank the touch area. Its role is still unsettled.
scenes.caption: So Pax6 may bias how markers are expressed more than it decides where an area sits. But in 2013, a cortex-only knockout shrank the touch area. Its role is still unsettled.
scenes.visual: Pax6 row verdict fills: loss and gain disagree; role in placing borders unsettled. On screen: 2013, smaller somatosensory area.
scenes.narration: So Pax6 may bias how markers are expressed more than it decides where an area sits. But in 2013, a cortex-only knockout shrank the touch area. Its role is still unsettled.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: when losing a factor and adding it move borders in opposite directions, that is the strongest evidence the factor helps allocate territory. A missing converse result does not rule a factor out.
scenes.visual: The finished table, showing the observed results: Emx2, opposite shifts; COUP-TFI, loss result only; Pax6, loss shifts markers, gain flat. On screen: strongest evidence, loss and gain in opposite directions.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: when losing a factor and adding it move borders in opposite directions, that is the strongest evidence the factor helps allocate territory. A missing converse result does not rule a factor out.
